message.content:
Yes—if you’re experiencing excessive or disruptive noise in Atlanta, you can file a complaint with the city’s authorities. Here’s how: | Step | What to Do | Where to Go | |------|------------|-------------| | **1** | Identify the source and time of the disturbance. | Gather details (date, time, location, description). | | **2** | Contact the Atlanta Police Department (APD) or the City of Atlanta’s Code Enforcement Office. | • APD: 404‑656‑4000 (non‑emergency line)
• Code Enforcement: 404‑656‑4000 (same line; ask for “Code Enforcement”) | | **3** | File a formal complaint. | • Call 311 (or 404‑656‑4000) and request a “Noise Complaint.”
• Or use the City of Atlanta’s online portal: https://www.atlantaga.gov/311 | | **4** | Provide all relevant information. | • Address, unit number, name of offending party (if known), and any evidence (audio recordings, photos). | | **5** | Follow up. | • You’ll receive a case number; keep it handy for future reference. | ### Quick Tips - **Non‑Emergency Line:** Use 404‑656‑4000 for non‑urgent matters; the dispatcher will route your call appropriately. - **Online Filing:** If you prefer digital, log in to the City’s 311 portal, select “Noise Complaint,” and fill out the form. - **Evidence Helps:** If you have recordings or witness statements, bring them when you file the complaint. Once filed, the city will investigate and may issue warnings, fines, or other enforcement actions depending on the severity and frequency of the noise violation.
